provenance: Regenerated by the leader (0-Main). The executor QA lane produced the generation 1-5 argv/lease/red-team scenarios below; the final-boundary lane was resumed as a read-only agent and reported executed=false rather than fabricating a reproduction, so the live-runtime scenarios here are the leader's own runs with archived logs named per scenario.

scenarios.scenario: Attempt to place a refused flag, its value, a blank value, or a separator-derived value on child argv. Covers --resume/--session-dir/--append-system-prompt/--system-prompt/--mode/-p/-r/-c/--fork/--no-session, unknown flags, inline = forms, --model= and whitespace-only inline values, --model '' standalone blanks, --model --, repeated selectors, and tokens after --.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: Refused fail-closed; no refused flag or value reaches the child; exactly one model flag ever present.
scenarios.observed: Cleared at generation 5 after four rounds. Root cause was two divergent definitions of a usable value; a single isBlankValue predicate now governs both the inline and separate-token forms. Executor lane ran 75 direct and 76 real-CLI cases plus all 25 trim-recognized Unicode whitespace code points with no leak in captured stub-argv.json.

scenarios.scenario: Concurrent and sequential attaches on separate connections, including an attach whose bind is still in flight.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: Exactly one holder; losers get session_lease_held with detail.holder populated.
scenarios.observed: Holds. The claim is synchronous, so a hanging bind still refuses a rival.

scenarios.scenario: Strand the origin: SIGKILL the holder, destroy the UDS with no protocol close, fail the attach after the claim, restart the daemon, and drop a connection while its bind is in flight.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: A later attach always succeeds; a stale bind never overwrites the newer holder's persisted session.
scenarios.observed: Holds after two fixes: a post-await lease-ownership re-check before putSession, and release hooks on unix close/error, stdio end/close and stop(). Accepted residual: SIGKILL of the wrapper leaves an orphan child (outside AC-6's contract; documented in docs/architecture.md).

scenarios.scenario: Drive or rotate the terminal origin from the chat surface via chat.send, /new, /reset, chat.react, engagement.reaction.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: Refused before the /new branch; no turn driven and no epoch bump.
scenarios.observed: Holds; epoch verified unchanged in SQLite. Reaction verbs keep refusing via their pre-existing platform gate.

scenarios.scenario: null, arrays, non-object params, argv: null, non-string argv entries, non-boolean reset, holder: null, non-numeric holder.pid, non-string holder.label.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: invalid_params before any lease is claimed; origin still free afterwards.
scenarios.observed: Holds after adding strict pre-claim validation.

scenarios.scenario: Piped stdin with the stub env unset, and the stub-env exemption.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: Refusal before connecting: no lease, no row, no child.
scenarios.observed: Holds. Confirmed against a real daemon: without a PTY the CLI prints the TTY refusal; under script -q /dev/null it proceeds to the connect step.

scenarios.scenario: Exit-code passthrough, signal forwarding, spawn-and-wait liveness, and a transport that dies before the child is spawned.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: Wrapper outlives the child, forwards signals, reports 128+N, and never spawns after transport death.
scenarios.observed: Holds; the pre-spawn race was found by the QA lane and fixed with a transportDead guard.

scenarios.scenario: Real daemon, real native gjc, no stub seam, PTY via script: two sequential gajaeway gjc invocations, then --new.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: Both invocations resume the same native session id; --new binds a new id at a higher epoch while the previous epoch directory and contents survive.
scenarios.observed: PASS after fixing a real defect the drill exposed. Initially every launch died with Session "<id>" not found because the binder injected the epoch dir as --session-dir while gjc sdk session raw rejects that flag. After removing the injection: 02fc31f1-f670-4eb0-a931-427f16c76a35 at e0 twice, 5f02cb5e-aadd-4094-bdf1-eab3015c3cdc at e1 after --new, e0 and its marker intact. Log: artifacts/gjc-entrypath-drill-log.txt. After the storage mechanism was corrected to pin an epoch-scoped native state root, the drill was re-run: sessions 02fc31f1-f670-4eb0-a931-427f16c76a35 at e0 (resumed by both sequential invocations) and 5f02cb5e-aadd-4094-bdf1-eab3015c3cdc at e1 after --new, with the native transcripts written to sessions/terminal/e0/agent/sessions/ and e1/agent/sessions/ respectively, and e0 plus its marker intact. AC-11 is therefore satisfied as written, not merely in narrowed form.

scenarios.scenario: Daemon and CLI given deliberately different GJC_CODING_AGENT_DIR values.
scenarios.expectedBehavior: The child resolves the store the daemon bound in; no Session not found.
scenarios.observed: Reproduced as a failure before the fix (stranded on every invocation). After transmitting the daemon's native-state decision totally (childEnv plus childEnvUnset, applied as a replacement): both invocations resumed 994f60b6-213c-4d5d-a66d-5a1f0b8b2e72 with the mismatch still in place; control resumed e9735b9d-b085-4603-aed4-f63ec321b646 twice. Log: artifacts/gjc-entrypath-scope-probe-log.txt. Superseded by a stronger fix: the gateway now DICTATES the native state root (epoch-scoped) to both the create and the child, so divergence is structurally impossible rather than corrected after the fact.

scenarios.scenario: gajaeway gjc --worktree probe-branch against real gjc under a PTY, with a valid fixture (git repo whose .gitignore excludes /.worktrees).
scenarios.expectedBehavior: Per the locked spec, --worktree works identically through gajaeway gjc.
scenarios.observed: SATISFIED, after a wrong first conclusion. Forwarding the flag is genuinely unsafe: native gjc enters a worktree it names itself (observed hazard-branch-f6ddf077) before resolving the session, so the bound session reads as a different project and the TUI offers 'Fork into current directory? [y/N]'; a control resuming the same session without the flag shows no prompt (artifacts/gjc-entrypath-worktree-hazard-log.txt). I initially concluded the flag was unsupportable, which was wrong - I had only shown that FORWARDING was unsafe. --worktree/-w are now wrapper-owned: the gateway prepares <workspace>/.worktrees/<branch> with plain 'git worktree add', binds the session with that cwd, and spawns the child there with no worktree flag. Verified live: two sequential 'gajaeway gjc --worktree probe-branch' invocations both resumed baaa782d-d826-47ce-885e-258c2cb97f71 with no fork prompt (artifacts/gjc-entrypath-scope-probe-log.txt). Derived rule: an epoch's cwd is fixed for its lifetime, recorded as bound-cwd in the epoch artifact directory, and an attach that would move the session is refused naming the remedy.

blockers: AC-8 wording vs mechanism. The worktree behavior is delivered and verified live (two sequential 'gajaeway gjc --worktree probe-branch' invocations resumed the same native session with no fork prompt), but the criterion's literal observable - the flag present in child argv - is not met. Routes A, B, D, F and H are measured and closed, with C as the control. Route E is rejected on architecture (replicating gjc's generated worktree suffix). Route G is unmeasured and would require seeding gjc onboarding state plus a two-phase attach that inverts the sole-binder invariant. Route I is PROMISING but incompletely measured: with the worktree created by gjc itself and the session still bound by the gateway inside it, resuming with the flag retained produced NO branch_in_use and NO fork prompt - the two failure modes that closed B and D - but the launch stalled in first-run onboarding, so no clean resume was observed. Route I would also depend on a throwaway non-interactive warm-up invocation per worktree. Full detail in artifacts/gjc-entrypath-worktree-hazard-log.txt sections A-I. The decision is the user's: ratify the wrapper-owned interpretation, reword AC-8, reject worktree support, or fund route I/G.
acceptedResiduals: SIGKILL of the gajaeway gjc wrapper leaves the already-spawned TUI running while the gateway frees the lease. Outside AC-6's contract (which requires only lease release for that case) and unavoidable without a parent-death hook the native runtime does not expose. Documented in docs/architecture.md with an operator action.
The stdio-transport and stop() lease-release hooks are asserted by construction rather than by a test that could fail, because the in-memory lease is discarded with the server runtime.
summary.verification: From artifacts/gjc-entrypath-verification-log.txt, which now captures exit codes rather than asserting them: bunx tsc --noEmit reported no diagnostics, exit 0; bun test packages = 1309 pass / 0 fail / 2 skip, Ran 1311 tests across 96 files; biome over the 17 changed .ts files found 1 warning, server.ts noNonNullAssertion, which is pre-existing debt outside the diff.
summary.ac11Status: pass (satisfied as written: native transcripts live inside the epoch directory)
summary.ac8Status: OPEN interpretation, not met as written. The behavior is delivered (--worktree <branch> puts the operator in a managed worktree with the persona session bound there, verified live), but AC-8's literal observable is that the flag appears unchanged in child argv, and it is deliberately consumed as wrapper-owned instead. Ratification is a user decision; see artifacts/gjc-entrypath-session-store-erratum.md section 2.
